records.body:
=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next round → the owner → the last ship sails → sail → talk → commit crew → commit trump → spend and strength → resolve the raid → score → bookkeeping → the reveal → after the last round.

4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.

At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.

[user]
=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). 8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.

4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).

The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). === Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). 9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).

7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). 9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

=== Loot: Sealed Raids ===

Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Each player starts with 30 crew (private: only you know your remaining crew), 0 gold, 3 unsailed merchant ships worth 3, 5 and 7 gold, 1 unused Captain and 1 unused Admiral. Players are seated 1 to N. The game lasts 3 x N rounds (12 with 4 players).

Each round:
1. Owner. The owner is player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1, so each player is owner exactly 3 times. The owner and the owner's unsailed ships are announced.
2. Sail. The owner privately chooses one of their unsailed ships to sail. If only one remains, it is sailed automatically. Its value is not revealed until the end of the round.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk binds no one.
4. Commit. At the same moment, every player secretly chooses a whole number of crew to commit, from 0 up to their remaining crew. At the same moment, the owner may declare their Admiral if it is unused, and each non-owner may declare their Captain if it is unused; you are only offered a trump you may legally declare. Invalid amounts are set to 0; invalid trump declarations are ignored.
5. Spend. Every player's committed crew is subtracted from their remaining crew, whatever the result (30 crew minus a commit of 10 leaves 20).
6. Strength. The owner's defense equals the crew they committed. Each attacker's strength equals the crew they committed, plus 6 if they declared their Captain this round.
7. Resolve, in this order: (a) If the owner declared the Admiral, the owner keeps the ship, whatever the attack. (b) Otherwise, find the highest attacker strength. The ship goes to that attacker only if their strength is strictly greater than the owner's defense and strictly greater than every other attacker's strength (attack 8 against defense 7 wins). (c) In every other case, including ties between the top attackers (even if they beat the defense) or an attack that does not beat the defense (attack 7 against defense 7 loses), the owner keeps the ship.
8. Score. Whoever gets the ship adds its value to their gold.
9. Bookkeeping. The ship is removed from the owner's unsailed ships. Declared trumps are marked used and cannot be declared again; an undeclared trump stays unused.
10. Announce. The ship's value, who got it, and who used a Captain or Admiral this round are revealed. No crew amounts are revealed.

End: after round 3 x N the game ends. Unspent crew is worth 0. The player with the most gold wins; players tied for the most gold share the result (a draw).
